follow100Note: Rows add up with a small rounding difference. Kept as profit is negative — the quarter lost money, so each $100 of revenue ended $8.76 in the red.
oneTimers: Share-based compensation, $272.5M (up from $176.3M a year ago): the largest non-GAAP add-back and the entire reason GAAP operating income is an $85.3M loss while non-GAAP operating income is $217.3M. It is excluded from non-GAAP results, but it is a real cost — it dilutes existing shareholders.

July 19 Incident costs, net, $21.0M (vs $0 a year ago): legal fees, remediation, sensor testing and related costs from the July 2024 outage, net of insurance receivables. A new charge this year; excluded from non-GAAP results.

Acquisition-related tax provision, $49.9M: the tax line is a $46.3M charge even though the quarter lost $46.5M before tax, because it includes this $49.9M acquisition-related provision (footnote 10). It is added back in the non-GAAP reconciliation.
Amortization of acquired intangible assets, $7.3M (vs $5.5M a year ago), and acquisition-related expenses, $1.5M: small, recurring non-GAAP add-backs as acquisitions flow in.
otherDetail: Interest income of $46.597M, less $6.664M of interest expense, plus other expense of $1.095M — net $38.838M. The tax line is a $46.268M charge on a $46.463M pre-tax loss, mostly a $49.883M acquisition-related provision, so the tax line deepened the loss instead of softening it.

takeaways.text: Net new ARR — new subscription value signed in the quarter — hit a record $224.3M, taking total ARR to $4.24B (+23% YoY). Subscription revenue grew 27% to $1.01B, and the newer Next-Gen SIEM, Cloud Security and Identity Protection businesses passed $1.3B in combined ARR. Customers keep consolidating on Falcon: 97% gross retention, and Falcon Flex deals added over $1B of in-quarter deal value.
takeaways.title: Record new business

takeaways.text: The GAAP operating loss was $85.3M, against a $29.7M profit a year ago — sales and marketing alone jumped 41% to $409.5M. Stock-based compensation of $272.5M is the whole gap: excluding it and smaller add-backs, operating income was $217.3M, a 21% margin. The underlying profit is real; shareholders pay for it in dilution.
takeaways.title: Operations lost money on a GAAP basis

takeaways.text: Operating cash flow of $345.7M and free cash flow of $239.8M still flowed — customers pay subscriptions upfront, so cash arrives long before the revenue is counted — and cash ended at $4.32B. But the $92.7M net loss was deepened by a $46.3M tax charge on a pre-tax loss, driven by a $49.9M acquisition-related provision. Non-GAAP EPS was $1.03; GAAP EPS was -$0.37.
takeaways.title: Cash flowed, but tax deepened the loss

verdict: CrowdStrike grew revenue 25% to $1.06B and signed a record $224M of net new subscriptions, but $273M of stock-based pay pushed the core business to an $85M operating loss — and a $46M tax charge on a pre-tax loss turned it into a $93M net loss, even as the business still generated $240M of free cash flow.
